ca_upper_canyon.blurb: Upper Canyon is a small bouldering pocket within the Potter's Point zone above Santa Barbara. It has nine problems on a couple of modest boulders, with a few much larger blocks further down the shallow canyon that have seen little development. The grades lean hard: one easy problem and one around V4, then four at V6, two at V7 and a single V9, so it suits strong boulderers more than beginners. The sandstone is coarse, which is typical for the neighbouring boulders at Potter's Point. To find it, head down the short path that runs alongside the canyon bed from Dan's Boulder.

ca_short_traverse_rock.blurb: Short Traverse Rock is one of the boulders at Grizzly Peak Boulders, a tree-covered bouldering spot in the Berkeley hills about ten minutes from the UC Berkeley campus. It is the lower of the rocks on the right-hand side of the group, and the walk in from the path takes about a minute. There are nine problems: slab warm-ups on the left, a few mantles around the corner, and a spread of harder lines up to V9, including two V8 traverses. The surrounding trees keep the area shaded, and the volcanic stone nearby is a little crumbly in places.

ca_platypus.blurb: Platypus is a freestanding sandstone tower, around 40 feet tall, in the Western Addition section of Castle Rock State Park in the Santa Cruz Mountains. It has nine routes: mostly bolted sport lines that can also be top-roped, plus one trad arete. Most of the climbing sits in the 5.10 range, with a couple of 5.11s and a 5.7 at the easy end. The style is slabby and technical: one side is low-angle, another holds the steeper lines, and one route sits in a gully. Bring quickdraws and little else.

ca_mount_lamarck.blurb: Mount Lamarck is the high point just north of Lamarck Col in the Evolution area of the High Sierra, with views across the Evolution Range from its top. The routes are alpine and trad climbs, mostly in the 5.10 to 5.11 range over several pitches, plus a snow and ice couloir on the north side at WI2 and a scramble line. Reaching the peak means a long approach: a trail from North Lake up to Upper Lamarck Lake, then user trail and cross-country travel to the col. This is a mountain day rather than a crag visit.

ca_north_pile.blurb: North Pile is the larger of the two small rock piles in the Entrance Piles group, in the Alabama Hills near Lone Pine. It has eight routes, nearly all trad with a few that can be top-roped. Grades are mostly easy to moderate: a 5.6, a cluster of 5.7s and 5.8s, a 5.9, and one 5.11 at the top end. The approach is a matter of minutes, so it fits easily into a day among the other small formations nearby.

ca_small_world_cliff.blurb: Small World Cliff is a small crag in Joshua Tree National Park, across the road from Sheep Pass Campground. It offers a handful of crack and face routes, mixing trad leads with a few top-rope lines. Grades run from 5.6 up to 5.12, with three lines at 5.10. The cliff is visible from the road, so the walk from the pullout is only a couple of hundred yards. The namesake crack is the best-known line, which makes this a convenient short outing when you are already working the Sheep Pass area.

ca_practice_boulder.blurb: Practice Boulder is one of a pair of roughly 12-foot boulders beside the road at the bottom of Mount Woodson, in north San Diego County. The one on the north side of the road carries the name, and the other sits directly opposite. There are eight climbs: mostly short boulder problems, with three in the easiest grade bracket and a couple of much harder ones, plus a 5.10 finger crack that can be led on gear. Because it is next to the road, it works as a quick warm-up stop before heading deeper into the Woodson boulders.

ca_wavy_gravy_wall.blurb: Wavy Gravy Wall is part of Horseshoe Piles, a group of small crags on steep wooded slopes above Horseshoe Lake near Mammoth Lakes, at roughly 9,200 feet. It combines technical steep face climbing with gentler slab lines on the right side. Most routes are bolted, with a couple of trad options, and the grades span 5.8 to 5.11, mostly 5.10 and 5.11. At this elevation the climbing season is short and tied to snow melt.
ca_wavy_gravy_wall.parking_note: Leave the car in the Lake George parking lot.
ca_wavy_gravy_wall.approach: Take the Crystal Lake Trail uphill for a few minutes to the big water tanks, then leave the trail westward, cross the ridge and contour along the slope beside the metal pipes to a stream. Spring Wall comes first; Wavy Gravy Wall is about 80 yards beyond it, up on the left.
